query eQTL catalogue credible sets

Source: R/coloc-query.R
query_eqtl_cat.Rd

This function takes an input credible set, uses that to define a region of interest, and searches for eQTL Catalogue credible sets that may overlap - ie contain at least one snp within the region +/- window. The resulting list of eQTL Catalogue credible sets may then be colocalised with the index credible set using the coloc_query() function.

Usage

query_eqtl_cat(
  cs,
  quant_method = "ge",
  window = 1e+05,
  version = .eqtl_cat_default_version
)

Arguments

cs

an index data.frame containing columns "chr" and "pos", for a single chromosome. chr may be numeric or character, eg 6, "6" or "X". Credible sets returned by query_ot() can be used directly.

quant_method

the eQTL Catalogue contains results for up to six different ways of quantifying gene expression: exon, ge, leafcutter, majiq, tx, txrev. See https://www.ebi.ac.uk/eqtl/Methods/. majiq is a recent splicing quantification that was introduced to eQTL Catalogue in r8, so is not available in r7. The default is ge, but you can choose more than one if you wish.

window

numeric value saying how far outside the index credible set we should search. Given that only overlapping credible sets can show colocalisation there is no reason to set this particularly large. The default, 1e+5, has been adequate in all our tests.

version

eQTL Catalogue release: "r8-beta" (default, https://zenodo.org/records/23398345) or "r7" (https://zenodo.org/records/23397994). Each release is kept in its own subdirectory of the cache directory.

Value

a list of credible sets with an attribute "annot" containing a data.frame where one row per element in the list describes the annotation of the list (most importantly, dataset_id).

Details

The eQTL Catalogue credible sets are stored, for each release and quantification method, as a series of files each covering a block of the genome. query_eqtl_cat() downloads only the file(s) overlapping the query region (typically one, ~25 MB per quantification method) to the cache dir, and reuses them in later queries. To download everything in advance, use eqtl_cat_fetch(). As for query_ot(), files are kept in the directory given by options(coloc.cache_dir = ...); see coloc-options. These files are the eQTL Catalogue's own credible sets, unchanged but split by genomic position: release r7 at https://zenodo.org/records/23397994 and r8-beta at https://zenodo.org/records/23398345.

See also

coloc_query(), eqtl_cat_fetch()

Author

Chris Wallace

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
q <- data.frame(chr = 6,
   pos = c(90279406, 90280331, 90281412, 90276601, 90288603, 90286261),
   snp = c("6_90279406_G_C", "6_90280331_G_A", "6_90281412_A_T",
           "6_90276601_A_G", "6_90288603_A_G", "6_90286261_C_G"),
   PP = c(0.675, 0.0747, 0.0702, 0.0505, 0.0422, 0.0412))

ecat <- query_eqtl_cat(q)
out2 <- coloc_query(q, ecat)
out2[out2$PP.H4 > 0, ]

ecat7 <- query_eqtl_cat(q, version = "r7") # an earlier release
} # }
